conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation and low drawdown. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, but still carries market risk, especially from remaining tech exposure. Expect tighter stops and a focus on stability over aggressive growth.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth with a blend of broad index and quality tech. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, but remains exposed to market swings. Drawdowns will be moderate compared to aggressive modes.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by leaning into leveraged ETFs and concentrated positions. This mode significantly amplifies both potential upside and drawdown, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is critical to manage the higher risk of substantial losses.

Cut all leveraged ETFs to zero

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF risk. Sell SMH to zero to remove high-beta semiconductor exposure. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration while maintaining broad market exposure. Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize income and monthly distributions. Trim QQQ to 10% to reduce growth exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, but distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs. This is for cash-like income, not a savings account, and still carries market risk.
